definitions.explanation: A person dressed entirely in black who assists performers on stage in kabuki or bunraku theater, conventionally treated as invisible by the audience.

definitions.gloss: behind-the-scenes person; someone who works unseen
definitions.explanation: By extension, someone who operates behind the scenes to make things happen, often without receiving public credit.

examples.japanese: {黒子|くろこ}が{小道具|こどうぐ}を{運|はこ}ぶ。
{歌舞伎|かぶき}の{黒子|くろこ}は{全身|ぜんしん}{黒|くろ}い{衣装|いしょう}を{着|き}ている。
examples.english: Kabuki stagehands wear entirely black costumes.

examples.japanese: {舞台|ぶたい}の{上|うえ}では{黒子|くろこ}は「{見|み}えない」ことになっている。
examples.english: On stage, the stagehands are conventionally treated as invisible.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はこのプロジェクトの{黒子|くろこ}だ。
examples.english: He's the one working behind the scenes on this project.

examples.japanese: {政治|せいじ}の{黒子|くろこ}として{暗躍|あんやく}する。
examples.english: To operate behind the scenes in politics.

examples.japanese: {成功|せいこう}の{裏|うら}には{多|おお}くの{黒子|くろこ}たちの{努力|どりょく}がある。
examples.english: Behind every success, there are the efforts of many unsung contributors.

notes:
Originally a kabuki theater term. The {黒子|くろこ} wears a full black costume including a hood, based on the convention that black represents invisibility on the traditional Japanese stage. This theatrical concept has become a widely used metaphor in everyday Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {黒子|くろこ}に{徹|てっ}する: to commit to working behind the scenes
- {黒子|くろこ}{役|やく}: behind-the-scenes role
- {政治|せいじ}の{黒子|くろこ}: political operator behind the scenes

NOTE ON READING:
The same kanji {黒子|ほくろ} can also be read ほくろ, meaning "mole" (the skin mark). Context makes the reading clear.

CULTURAL NOTE:
The convention of "invisible" stagehands reflects a unique aspect of Japanese theater aesthetics — the audience agrees to ignore their presence, even though they are in plain sight. This cultural concept extends to the figurative use.
